header:
MORNING MONEY
GM buys itself back

lines.text: GM plans to spend $20 billion buying its own stock.
lines.say: GM plans to spend twenty billion dollars buying its own stock.

lines.text: Here's what a buyback really does, and who it touches.
lines.say: Here's what a buyback really does, and who it touches.

lines.text: It came with a strong quarter: July-September profit of $3.3 billion, up from $1.3 billion a year earlier.
lines.say: It came with a strong quarter: July through September profit of three point three billion dollars, up from one point three billion a year earlier.

lines.text: In a buyback, a company buys its own shares, so each remaining share owns a bigger slice.
lines.say: In a buyback, a company buys its own shares, so each remaining share owns a bigger slice.

lines.text: GM's been at it for years: about 1.2 billion shares at the end of 2023, 849 million by September 2026.
lines.say: GM's been at it for years, from about one point two billion shares at the end of 2023 to eight hundred forty-nine million by September 2026.

lines.text: That $20 billion is about six times GM's third-quarter profit.
lines.say: That twenty billion is about six times GM's third-quarter profit.

lines.text: The catch: that cash leaves the company, and GM says it can pause the plan anytime.
lines.say: The catch? That cash leaves the company, and GM says it can pause the plan anytime.

lines.text: Fewer shares is why profit per share can climb even when total profit doesn't.
lines.say: Fewer shares is why profit per share can climb even when total profit doesn't.

post.title: GM approved a $20B buyback. Here's what it does
post.ig:
GM plans to spend $20 billion buying its own stock.
GM announced a new $20 billion buyback with no end date on Oct 20, 2026.
GM earned $3.3 billion in Q3 2026, up from $1.3 billion a year earlier.
Its share count fell from about 1.2 billion at the end of 2023 to 849 million by Sept 30, 2026.
Sources: GM Q3 2026 earnings release and 2025 10-K.
